  Terse gloss: "Zerahiah; a priestly name meaning 'Yah has risen/shone,' in Aaronide genealogies and among returning exiles"
  Readable gloss: "A masculine proper noun meaning 'the LORD has risen' or 'the LORD has shone,' combining zeraḥ ('rising, shining') with the divine name. Zerahiah appears in the Aaronide priestly genealogy as a descendant of Eleazar and ancestor of Ezra (1 Chr 6:6, 51; Ezra 7:4). In Ezra 8:4 a Zerahiah heads a family among the returning exiles, possibly the same individual or a descendant. The Septuagint consistently renders it Zaraia."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: ""
    Enriched: A theophoric personal name borne by priests in the Aaronide line. Attested in the genealogy running from Eleazar through to Ezra (1 Chr 6:6, 51; Ezra 7:4) and as a family head among returning exiles (Ezra 8:4). The name's meaning — 'Yah has risen/shone' — connects it to the South Arabian cognate ḏrḥʾl. Spanish 'Zerajya/Zeraḥyah' and the LXX Ζαραια all preserve the theophoric element.
    Existing Spanish translations: Zerajya, Zeraĥyah, Zeraḥyah, y-Zerajya
